name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.204.0 — Genesis design stage gains the kit and the journey stories (specs/20260926/05): after the design brief, DESIGN_KIT has Fable author tokens, shell and one composite per pattern row with a story per declared state, installs Storybook by a printed recipe, and kit-landed runs the contract check, requires .storybook/main.*, builds Storybook and requires iframe.html plus a state story per declared state; DESIGN_JOURNEYS writes a beats file per seed journey, and journeys-drawn requires one journey story per journey that imports its beats and calls step(), bans primitive imports under the journeys directory, and finds a journey+play-fn entry per journey in the rebuilt index. HANDOFF stamps design {kit, tokens, rules}. 7.203.0 — Genesis gains the DESIGN_BRIEF state after the zero-day gate is green: a web host now writes docs/design/brief.md and fills the host's rules tables under Fable, catalog-inventory.js derives the installed catalog inventory the driver verifies mechanically, a design-brief skill and brief/paths templates ship the workbench, design-contract-check.js gains overrides for the new state, and the gray mock app stops auto-picking the stack or skipping the scaffold — genesis always picks and scaffolds, reading the mock app's approval record for the last time at this state's entry. 7.202.0 — Gates, per workspace: /spec:enforce now discovers and wires enforcers once per workspace, not once per repo — a new workspace-scan.js walks the tree for package manifests, the enforce cell grammar gains workspace (and, for naming, a layer of code/schema/routes/wire), and the grounding contract's Rule enforcement section states the (workspace x stack x category) entry shape and id grammar; a monorepo with a Python API and a TypeScript frontend now gets its own checker set per workspace, with naming enforced per layer from the host naming table, and every checker wired to run from its own workspace root inside the one gate string.
